title: Vivot
description: Vivot is a civic participation prototype seeking support to become a reliable public-interest product for real-world use.
heroLede: Vivot already shows how petitions and polls can feel simpler and clearer. To turn this prototype into a secure product people can truly use, we are actively looking for support, partners, and institutional contacts, especially in government and municipalities.
microSupportText: If you work in government, a municipality, or a public institution, we would be glad to hear from you.
panelNoteTitle: If you work in government, research, or public funding:
panelNoteText: This project is looking for the right support to grow from prototype to usable public-interest infrastructure. We would be glad to talk.
missionCardTwoTitle: A simple app for petitions and polls.
missionCardTwoText: Later, ideally with stronger identity and e-ID support.
missionCardThreeText: Especially from government, municipalities, foundations, research, and other public institutions.
storyOneTitle: Still a prototype. But a serious one.

privacyPolicy.title: Privacy Policy - Stimmapp
privacyPolicy.heading: Privacy Policy
privacyPolicy.intro: Trainvent provides the Stimmapp service. This page explains the general privacy rules for the app and links to the specific notice for crash diagnostics.
privacyPolicy.overviewPurpose: When you use Stimmapp, we process personal data only as needed to provide and improve the service, secure accounts, respond to support requests, and meet legal obligations.
privacyPolicy.overviewAds: Stimmapp does not show advertising, does not use advertising networks, and does not process personal data for personalized ads or ad measurement.
privacyPolicy.overviewData: This can include account details you provide directly, technical data needed to operate the app, and information generated while you use app features. Some processing is handled by third-party providers such as Google Play Services and Firebase products.
privacyPolicy.noticesIntro: The privacy information is split into these parts:
privacyPolicy.thirdParties: Stimmapp may use third-party services that process data on our behalf or as independent providers in connection with core app functionality. These services are not used to serve ads in Stimmapp.
privacyPolicy.providers: We may work with service providers to host infrastructure, authenticate users, store content, deliver support, detect abuse, and measure app stability. They may access personal data only as needed to provide those services.
privacyPolicy.security: We use commercially reasonable safeguards to protect personal data. No method of transmission or storage is perfectly secure, so absolute security cannot be guaranteed.
privacyPolicy.links: The app or website may link to third-party sites. Their privacy practices are governed by their own policies.
privacyPolicy.children: The service is not directed to children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect personal data from children under 13.
privacyPolicy.changes: We may update this page from time to time. Material changes will be published on this page together with an updated effective date.
privacyPolicy.contact: If you have questions about this Privacy Policy, contact

privacyPolicyCrashData.title: Privacy Policy: Crash Data - Stimmapp
privacyPolicyCrashData.heading: Privacy Policy: Crash Data
privacyPolicyCrashData.intro: This notice explains how Stimmapp handles crash diagnostics and similar technical error data.
privacyPolicyCrashData.data: If the app crashes or behaves unexpectedly, technical diagnostics may include device model, operating system version, app version, time of the error, approximate diagnostics about app state, and identifiers needed to distinguish repeated failures.
privacyPolicyCrashData.purpose: We use crash data to detect errors, reproduce problems, improve stability, prevent abuse, and make the app more reliable.
privacyPolicyCrashData.choice: Stimmapp provides a Privacy Settings control for crash logs. You can enable or disable sending crash logs there at any time. If the setting is shown as enabled, crash diagnostics may be sent when an app error occurs.
privacyPolicyCrashData.providers: Crash diagnostics may be processed through Firebase services or similar technical infrastructure providers used to run and monitor the app.
privacyPolicyCrashData.retention: Crash diagnostics are retained only for as long as reasonably needed for stability analysis, debugging, security, and operational documentation.

formImport.title: Import forms with JSON or PDF — Vivot
formImport.description: Import petitions and polls with JSON or PDF: instructions, examples and format requirements.
formImport.heading: Import premade forms
formImport.intro: Prepare a petition or poll as JSON or a PDF with selectable text. Import it into your draft, check the content and settings, and publish after review.
steps: Download an example below, or use a file someone has shared with you. Save it as a UTF-8 text file ending in .json.
In the app, open the petition or poll creator that matches the file type.
Open the import selector using the upload icon, choose “Import JSON form” and select your file.
Confirm replacing the included draft fields. Check the content, tags, duration, geographical scope, selected group and any image.
Edit as needed, then use the normal publication review to publish. Importing alone does not publish the form.
formImport.exampleHint: Edit the text and answer options in a text editor. Keep the field names and fixed values in English, even when your form is in another language.
fields: Required: petition, poll or survey. Must match the editor; the poll editor also accepts survey.
Required for polls/surveys; omit for petitions. 1–20 objects, each with title (1–200 characters) and an optional type: multipleChoice (default) or text.
For multipleChoice: required list of 2–10 distinct strings, each 1–50 characters; answers must differ ignoring letter case. For text: omit options or use an empty list []. null is not accepted.
Optional: 1–3 distinct keys from the tag list below.
Optional: true or false. true keeps the form open until you close it.
Optional: global, countryUnion, country, stateOrRegion or city.
Required for countryUnion scope: EU or UN. Omit for every other scope.
formImport.settings: Omitted optional fields keep their current draft values. The selected group audience and petition image also stay unchanged. Geography comes from your own profile; unavailable state or country-union scopes are rejected. Account IDs, votes, signatures, images and publication status cannot be imported.
formImport.errors: The file must be one JSON object, at most 256 KiB. Use double quotes, no comments and no trailing commas. Unknown fields, unsupported versions and values outside the limits are rejected. Text is trimmed before length checks. Start with an example and check the field named in the error. If a scope is unavailable, update your profile or choose an available scope.
formImport.questionTypes: Mix multipleChoice and text questions in the same poll. Multiple-choice questions let participants select one option. Text questions accept a written answer of up to 2,000 characters. Every question requires an answer. Written responses are visible only to the creator. Question type defaults to multipleChoice when omitted, so existing version 1 files still work.
formImport.exports: For a finished poll, use its save or share action and choose CSV, JSON or PDF. Exports include choice labels and written answers in question order. You can include the form content as well. These are result reports, not reusable form files: to import a new draft, use the version 1 format above. Written responses are included in the file you save or share.
formImport.pdfIntro: Use a simple PDF with selectable text in reading order. Scanned or image-only PDFs are not supported. Avoid columns, tables, headers and footers that interrupt the text.
pdfSteps: Open the petition or poll creator, tap the upload icon and choose “Import PDF”.
Select the PDF, then review and correct the extracted text before confirming.
Apply it to your draft, check the settings and use the usual publication review. Importing alone does not publish it.
pdfRules: First non-empty line: title (5–100 characters). All following lines before the first question form the description (20–1,000 characters). Blank lines are ignored.
For petitions, everything after the title is the description. Do not include poll questions.
For polls, start each question on a new line with a number, a dot or closing parenthesis, and a space: “1. Your question” or “2) Your question”. Use 1–20 questions with titles of 1–200 characters.

Put each choice on its own line with a letter and dot or closing parenthesis, or a bullet (-, •, ☐ or □), followed by a space. Use 2–10 distinct choices of 1–50 characters each. Case alone does not make them different.
A question without choices accepts a written answer. Unmarked continuation lines extend the preceding question or the last choice. Check wrapped text carefully.
Maximum: 10 MiB, 50 pages and 100,000 extracted text characters. Content must meet the same limits as JSON.
PDF imports include only the title, description and poll questions. Set tags, duration and geographical scope in the app. Your selected audience and petition image stay unchanged.
formImport.pdfExample:
Neighbourhood park improvements
Help us decide how to improve our neighbourhood park.

1. Which improvement should come first?
a) More trees
b) More benches

2. What else would you suggest?
formImport.pdfErrors: If no text is found, export the original document as a PDF with selectable text. If the format is rejected, correct the extracted text and check the title, description, question and choice limits. Result reports are not formatted for automatic reimport.
